title: Traffic-related air pollution and respiratory symptoms among asthmatic children, resident in Mexico City: the EVA cohort study.
ehr_evidence: Information concerning allergy test results, medication, and medical visits during the 2 preceding years was obtained from the medical record. The study primarily relied on daily symptom diaries, environmental monitoring stations (RAMA), and traffic counts.
summary: Prospective longitudinal panel study evaluating the association between traffic-related air pollution and respiratory symptoms/medication use among asthmatic and healthy children in Mexico City.
key_findings: An increase of 17.4 μg/m3 (IQR) in PM2.5 was associated with an 8.8% increase in wheezing (95% CI: 2.4% to 15.5%).
An increase of 34 ppb (IQR) in NO2 was associated with a 9.1% increase in wheezing (95% CI: 2.3% to 16.4%).
An increase of 48 ppb (IQR) in O3 was associated with a 10% increase in wheezing (95% CI: 3.2% to 17.3%).
Diesel-fueled vehicles were significantly associated with wheezing (IRR = 1.29; 95% CI: 1.03 to 1.62) and bronchodilator use (IRR = 1.32; 95% CI: 0.99 to 1.77) per 130 vehicles hourly increase.
Asthmatic children had a 3-fold higher incidence of coughing (IRR = 3.1) and 8.5-fold higher incidence of wheezing (IRR = 8.5) compared to healthy children.
Among healthy children, only NO2 was significantly associated with coughing (OR = 1.22; 95% CI: 1.03 to 1.45).
captured_features: daily symptom diaries (coughing, wheezing, breathing difficulty)
traffic density and vehicle type counts
data_source_type: environmental monitoring, daily symptom diaries, traffic counts, questionnaires
population: 147 asthmatic and 50 healthy children aged 6-14 years residing in Mexico City
exposure_domain: traffic-related air pollution (PM2.5, NO2, O3, diesel exhaust, traffic density)
limitations: exposure assessed via fixed-site monitors potentially causing misclassification
voluntary recruitment not representative of general pediatric population
small subsample for PM2.5 absorbance analysis
high correlation between traffic vehicle types complicating effect separation
